name: Tessford Tenant Stability Ordinance 2027
stated_aim: to protect Tessford's tenants from displacement and to allow long-standing residents, especially older residents, to remain in their homes and in their community

components.cap_unit: yearly increase (60% of the consumer price index change), from the base rent
source_sentences: The rent of a sitting tenant may rise by no more than 60 per cent of the annual change in the regional consumer price index in any twelve months, from the base rent.
On a new tenancy the landlord may set the initial rent.
A tenancy may not be assigned; a sublet needs the landlord's consent and may not be at more than the tenant's rent.
The ordinance was introduced on 1 March 2027, adopted on 11 May 2027 and takes effect on 1 October 2027.
funded by an annual fee of $90 per covered unit paid by the landlord and not recoverable from tenants.
In November 2026 a majority of the newly elected council and the mayor campaigned on rent regulation.

unclear.text: Whether displaced seniors also receive the Portable Senior Credit (section 7 against section 9, relocation payment in full settlement).
readings: U1-a: a senior who leaves on a withdrawal notice vacates the unit and keeps the credit as well as the $12,000
U1-b: the relocation payment settles all claims under the Ordinance, the credit included

context: Tessford's market rents rose about 6% a year in 2021 to 2026; the regional consumer price index rose about 3% a year.
Across the county line, 18 km east, is Durnside (Selcombe County; about 11,000 rental homes, no rent regulation), 22 minutes from central Tessford by rail.
